topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture series, outlines the key learning objectives, and sets the scope for exploring cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Environmental Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, contrasting intrinsic random mutations with extrinsic environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and the Burkitt Lymphoma Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents and pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as an in-depth case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical agents induce DNA damage directly or via metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Multi-Stage Carcinogenesis, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing cooperate with mutational initiation to facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic and evaluate human risk.
